research.label: Dogs Trust: enrichment ideas for bored dogs

substitutes: No jar? Use a mug or a hat.
optionalSupplies: A small treat reward from your dog's regular food
variations: Home version: slips for the yard, balcony, hallway or window, one rainy-day pick.
Seated version: only benches and viewpoints that need a short, flat walk.
Quiet version: only low-traffic spots and early-morning times.
No-car version: keep every slip within a ten-minute walk.
title: Saturday Morning Mystery
clue: Five folded slips sit in a jar, and none of them knows which one gets picked.
reveal: Mid-week, you write a few pre-checked local ideas on slips of paper. On Saturday morning you draw one blind and go. Your dog holds a veto: if they are not keen, you draw again.
objective: Draw a pre-checked local outing at random and enjoy it together, with your dog holding a veto.
instructions: Mid-week, write five to six slips of paper, each naming a dog-friendly local idea within an easy trip: a street you have never walked, the far corner of a park, a quiet square, a viewpoint, a lakeside path on leash.

Check each idea in advance: dogs allowed, leash rules, opening hours, ground and shade. The owner confirms any shop, cafe or garden allows dogs, or leaves it out. Every slip must be a good outing in the weather you will have.
Add one wildcard slip: 'follow your dog's nose for twenty minutes, where it is safe'. Fold all slips and put them in a jar.
On Saturday morning, pour a drink, call your dog and draw one slip without looking at the others. Read it out loud in your best announcer voice.
Veto rule: if your dog hangs back, wants to turn around or seems uneasy at the spot, you may redraw once, no questions asked.
Go and enjoy it for an hour or two, with water, waste bags and a short rest in the middle. Head home when your dog has had enough.
Drop the used slip in a 'done' envelope and write a fresh idea to refill the jar for next time.
twist: Chance picks the plan, your dog holds a veto, and the jar refills every week.
completion: Counts once a slip has been drawn and you have spent time at the spot, including when a veto swaps it.
photoIdea: Your dog beside the jar with the drawn slip, or the first moment at the chosen place, caught naturally.
memoryPrompt: What did the jar choose, and did your dog use the veto?

reservation.note: Check each slip first. The owner must confirm that any shop, cafe or garden allows dogs; leave it off if unsure.

safety: Check every slip in advance for dog rules, hours, shade and ground, and keep your dog leashed where required.
Honor the veto: go home or choose a quieter slip if your dog is uneasy, tired or too warm or cold.
Leash near any water, no swimming unless it is safe and your dog wants to; never leave your dog tied up outside a venue.

keepsake.headline: SATURDAY MYSTERY
keepsake.explainer: The jar chose. My dog held the veto

teaser: A jar, a few folded slips and a Saturday morning with no plan except the one you draw.
